A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HEEGNet and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original hyperbolicity measurements, EEG classification experiments, alignment ablations, runtime measurements, and fully hyperbolic architecture experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The hybrid Euclidean–hyperbolic architecture, two-stage DSMDBN alignment, HHSW training objective, and source-free adaptation procedure are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 and Table 6.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same visual-evoked-potential, emotion-recognition, intracranial EEG, and motor-imagery datasets and tasks. Section 4 and Appendix E retain identical coverage.

E2.justification: The general EEG, task-specific, foundation-model, and manifold baselines retain the same membership in their corresponding comparisons, including the EA and STMA combinations.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, cross-subject/cross-session evaluation, cross-validation schemes, 80/20 source splits, 100-epoch training budgets, and balanced-accuracy evaluation remain unchanged. No additional experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the alignment-component ablation in Table 4, t-SNE analysis in Figure 2, runtime comparison in Appendix D.4, and progressive replacement of Euclidean components in Appendix F.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting, domain counts, 10,000-permutation paired tests, and stated t-max corrections are unchanged. No repeated-run or seed information is added.

E6.justification: The main-text and appendix result entries and findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports overall balanced accuracy of 81.7 ± 14.4% for HEEGNet with DSMDBN+EA in both versions.

T1.justification: Definitions, axioms, assumptions, and mathematical arguments are retained. Appendix C.2 makes the mixed x/y and p/q notation consistent in Equation (17) and surrounding prose; the intended Euclidean construction and reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about EEG hyperbolicity, improved generalization, the hybrid architecture, two-stage alignment, and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of moment versus distribution alignment and the hybrid architecture remain unchanged. The computational-cost limitation and proposed future work are also retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete HEEGNet code-repository URL and code-availability statement to the abstract. Implementation, hyperparameter, software, and hardware disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: Appendix B.1 removes the SPD/Grassmann examples and Nguyen (2022) citation, whose bibliography entry is also removed. Definition B.3 adds the already-cited Ungar (2022) as a joint attribution. The main research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized appendix prose and notation edits, adds the abstract code sentence and corresponding-author footnote, and separates a paragraph in Section 4.2. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Red and blue main-text passages become black, and the added abstract sentence and footnote cause limited page reflow. Figures, table structures, and captions remain unchanged; Appendix D.4 retains its red text.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves usability and clarity by providing a concrete code location, resolving inconsistent notation in Appendix C.2, and cleaning up main-text formatting. These are limited benefits: the method, experimental support, conclusions, and limitations remain unchanged.
